title: Simple image of top-to-bottom line cohomology maps
statement:
Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field of characteristic $p>0$ [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure], and let $S$ be a semisimple simply connected $F$-group scheme [def-sc-group-scheme], with these terms as defined in [lem-sfb-rho-section-modules]. Fix a split maximal torus $T\subseteq B\subseteq S$, with $B$ a Borel subgroup, and use $X=X^*(T)$, roots $\Phi$, positive roots $\Phi^+$ in $\operatorname{Lie}(B)$, simple roots $\Delta$, coroots and their pairing from [lem-sfb-reductive-borel-pair-structure]. Let $B^-$ be the Borel opposite to $B$ relative to $T$, so its roots are $-\Phi^+$. Put $\rho=\frac12\sum_{\alpha\in\Phi^+}\alpha\in X$, $Q=\mathbf Z\Phi$, and $W=N_S(T)(F)/T(F)$, acting on $X$ by normalizer conjugation. Set $w\mathbin\cdot x=w(x+\rho)-\rho$, let $w_0\Phi^+=-\Phi^+$, and put $N=|\Phi^+|$. A rational module for any group here is an $F$-vector space with a coassociative counital coaction into its tensor product with that group's coordinate algebra; a submodule is a coaction-stable subspace. For $x\in X$, let $F_x$ be the one-dimensional $B^-$-module on which $T$ acts by $x$ and the unipotent radical acts trivially. For a finite-dimensional rational $B^-$-module $M$, let $\mathcal L(M)$ be the sheaf of sections of $S\times^{B^-}M$ on $S/B^-$: over $V\subseteq S/B^-$ its sections are regular maps $f:\pi^{-1}(V)\to M$ with $f(gb)=b^{-1}f(g)$, where $\pi:S\to S/B^-$ is the quotient. Write $H^i(M)=H^i(S/B^-,\mathcal L(M))$ for Zariski sheaf cohomology, with its natural left $S$-action, and $H^i(x)=H^i(F_x)$; set $H^i=0$ for $i<0$. Equivariance means a coaction identity, hence holds after every commutative $F$-algebra extension. A simple module is nonzero with no proper nonzero rational submodule, and a simple constituent means a simple subquotient. For $x\in X$ dominant, meaning $\langle x,\alpha^\vee\rangle\ge0$ for all $\alpha\in\Delta$, the nonzero module $H^0(x)$ has a unique simple submodule, denoted $L(x)$, whose highest weight for the positive Borel $B$ is $x$. Here highest weight means the character on the one-dimensional subspace fixed by the unipotent radical of $B$, as in [lem-sfb-simple-module-dual-highest-weight]. With the contragredient action on the linear dual, every nonzero $S$-linear map
$$H^N(w_0\mathbin\cdot x)\longrightarrow H^0(x)$$
has image $L(x)$. If $x+\rho$ is dominant but $x$ is not dominant, $H^0(x)=0$. The image assertion holds in rank zero as well. No nonvanishing of a particular comparison map is asserted.

source.place: Highest-weight properties of H^0 in the paragraph Weyl modules and cohomology groups, p.55; Lemma 4 and its Serre-duality proof, p.58. The top module is dual to H^0(-w_0 x) and has unique simple quotient L(x); the conclusion concerns maps between these two specific modules, not a categorical block decomposition.

proof.text: Choose a normalizer element $n$ conjugating $B$ to $B^-$ using [lem-sfb-torus-normalizer-borel-transitivity]. Conjugation carries the root spaces of the first Borel to those of the second, so its Weyl element sends $\Phi^+$ to $-\Phi^+$ and is $w_0$. Thus $nUn^{-1}=U^-$, and $n$ carries a $U$-fixed vector of weight $z$ to a $U^-$-fixed vector of weight $w_0z$. The reverse holds as $w_0^2=1$ by [lem-sfb-rho-regular-weyl-orbit]. We will use this also on duals. Torus coactions split into weights: writing $c(v)=\sum_a v_a\otimes t^a$ in Laurent monomials, coassociativity and the counit give $c(v_a)=v_a\otimes t^a$ and $v=\sum_a v_a$. This proves that taking a specified weight space preserves surjections of finite-dimensional rational $T$-modules.

source.place: 22.15 and 22.18–22.20, pp.466–468; conjugation and Laurent-coaction details written by NW

proof.text: For any finite-dimensional rational $S$-module $V$, evaluation at $1$ gives an injective linear map $\operatorname{Hom}_S(V,H^0(z))\to\operatorname{Hom}_{B^-}(V,F_z)$. Indeed $a(v)=\phi(v)(1)$ satisfies $a(bv)=z(b)a(v)$, and equivariance recovers $\phi(v)(g)=a(g^{-1}v)$. Conversely this formula is regular by the rational action, satisfies $\phi(v)(gb)=z(b)^{-1}\phi(v)(g)$, and is $S$-equivariant. The function-space identification is exactly [lem-sfb-flag-cohomology-finite-exact]. A functional $a$ is $B^-$-linear to $F_z$ precisely when it is a $U^-$-fixed vector of weight $-z$ in $V^\vee$. All formulas are identities after every scalar extension, not just on $F$-points.

source.place: 22.29–22.30, pp.470–471: Frobenius reciprocity, with both formulas verified explicitly

proof.text: Suppose $x$ is dominant. The dominant-character node supplies a finite-dimensional module with a nonzero $B$-eigenvector $v$ of weight $x$. Replace it by the rational submodule $C$ generated by $v$. The cyclic weight bound says $C_x=Fv$. Choose a proper rational submodule $K$ of largest dimension. It cannot contain $v$, so $J=C/K$ is simple with a nonzero $U$-fixed vector of weight $x$. The simple-module node says $J^U$ is a line, hence its highest weight is $x$, and $J^\vee$ is simple of highest weight $-w_0x$. Step 1 gives in $J^\vee$ a $U^-$-fixed line of weight $-x$. A nonzero vector on it is a $B^-$-map $J\to F_x$, and step 2 embeds $J$ in $H^0(x)$: its kernel is a proper submodule of the simple $J$. Thus $H^0(x)\ne0$; it is finite-dimensional by the flag-cohomology node.

source.place: 22.17–22.20 and 22.27, pp.467–470; explicit matrix-coefficient construction via 22.29

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-induced-module-primitive-line] with Borel $B^-$ and character $x$. Its longest element is again $w_0$, so $H^0(x)^{U^-}$ is one-dimensional of weight $w_0x$. Every simple submodule $J'$ has a nonzero $U^-$-fixed line by [lem-sfb-simple-module-dual-highest-weight] applied with Borel $B^-$. That line must be this same line. Two simple submodules therefore have a nonzero intersection and are equal. Step 3 supplies one; call it $L(x)$. Conjugating its invariant line by $n^{-1}$ shows that its positive highest weight is $x$. This proves existence, uniqueness and the stated highest weight, without using the linkage node above this item. It applies equally to the dominant weight $a=-w_0x$: the map $-w_0$ permutes the positive coroots and hence preserves dominance.

Put $a=-w_0x$, $A=H^0(a)$ and $D=H^N(w_0\mathbin\cdot x)$. Since $w_0\rho=-\rho$, we have $w_0\mathbin\cdot x=w_0x-2\rho$ and $-(w_0\mathbin\cdot x)-2\rho=a$. The perfect invariant pairing of [lem-sfb-flag-line-equivariant-serre-pairing], with $i=N$, identifies $D$ with $A^\vee$, for the contragredient action: $\langle gd,ga'\rangle=\langle d,a'\rangle$. Restriction of functionals to the submodule $L(a)\subseteq A$ is an equivariant surjection $A^\vee\to L(a)^\vee$ (extend a basis of $L(a)$ to one of $A$). The simple-module duality node gives highest weight $-w_0a=x$ for $L(a)^\vee$, so it is isomorphic to $L(x)$. Composing this surjection and isomorphism with $L(x)\hookrightarrow H^0(x)$ gives a nonzero map $q:D\to H^0(x)$ with image $L(x)$.

source.place: Contragredient paragraph p.471; Serre-duality input for Andersen Lemma 4 p.58 (article not local; assembly by NW)

proof.text: For $D=A^\vee$, step 2 injects $\operatorname{Hom}_S(D,H^0(x))$ into $(D^\vee)^{U^-}_{-x}$. Evaluation identifies $D^\vee$ with $A$ equivariantly in finite dimension. The primitive-line node with Borel $B^-$ and character $a$ gives $A^{U^-}$ one-dimensional of weight $w_0a=-x$. Consequently the Hom space has dimension at most one. The nonzero $q$ of step 5 spans it; every nonzero map is $c q$ with $c\in F^\times$ and has exactly the same image $L(x)$. This supplies the missing argument that a unique head and a unique socle by themselves would not supply.

source.place: 22.22 and 22.29–22.30, pp.469–471; map-space dimension argument by NW

proof.text: Finally assume $x+\rho$ is dominant while $x$ is not. Some simple coroot has $r=\langle x,\alpha^\vee\rangle<0$. Since $r$ is an integer and $\langle\rho,\alpha^\vee\rangle=1$, dominance of $x+\rho$ gives $r\ge-1$, hence $r=-1$. Apply the final vanishing clause of [lem-sfb-minimal-parabolic-line-cohomology] with the one-dimensional trivial $P_\alpha$-module $V=F$ and $\mu=x$ to get $H^0(x)=0$. If the root system is empty there is no such nondominant $x$; the preceding image proof still works: $N=0$, $w_0=1$, and the pairing and invariant-line assertions explicitly allow rank zero. No comparison map is assumed nonzero.

source.place: Boundary case of Andersen Lemma 4 p.58, from its rank-one vanishing input; numerical argument by NW
